In Xochimilco, city streets give way to canals and green riverbanks. Visitors travel aboard trajineras, wide boats with brightly painted sides and canopies. From the water, you can see gardens and everyday life in this Mexico City district.

A canal cruise is part of itineraries exploring the southern outskirts of the capital. The outing can be combined with visits to other Mexico City neighborhoods, while Xochimilco itself offers the chance to spend part of the day on the water.

Xpuhil is located in Campeche and is associated with ancient Maya settlements. Its architecture belongs to the Río Bec region. Particularly striking is a structure with 3 tall stone towers rising above the lower part of the building, illustrating a local approach to decorating monumental facades.

The complex adds to an exploration of the archaeological sites of southern Yucatán. Here you can examine the stone masonry and the layout of the buildings and compare them with other Maya cities. A visit to Xpuhil is often combined with Calakmul, highlighting the differences in architectural traditions and the natural surroundings of ancient settlements.
